title: ImageDoubler: image-based doublet identification in single-cell sequencing
concrete_content: Uses retained Fluidigm cell images to identify doublets with reported performance up to 93.87% and exposes limits of transcriptome-simulated doublet benchmarks.
decision_changed: Makes image availability part of the QC contract and prevents generalizing an image-based result to ordinary droplet data.
constraints: Requires retained Fluidigm imaging; does not validate a 10x transcriptome-only doublet method or address ambient RNA.
skill_action: Ask for image provenance; audit doublet attrition and hybrid-marker sensitivity; mark the general droplet benchmark gap.
writing_requirement: Methods: image acquisition, classifier and threshold; Results: performance and attrition; Legend: image/score definition; Discussion: platform-limited generalizability.

title: A comprehensive analysis framework for evaluating commercial single-cell RNA sequencing technologies
concrete_content: Compares nine commercial scRNA-seq kits on PBMCs for read utilization, sensitivity, cost and analytic performance.
decision_changed: Requires platform/read-utilization and cost-sensitivity reporting instead of treating cell count as the only assay-quality metric.
constraints: Single PBMC donor and time-specific product versions; cannot establish a universal best kit.
skill_action: Match assay choice to estimand; audit per-sample yield and retained-information metrics; request kit/version metadata.
writing_requirement: Methods: kit/version, input, depth and pipeline; Results: sensitivity/read utilization; Legend: donor and depth; Discussion: single-donor/product-version limits.

title: Uncovering functional lncRNAs by scRNA-seq with ELATUS
concrete_content: Benchmarks alignment, reference annotation and filtering for low-expression lncRNA recovery and implements Kallisto-based ELATUS with selective filtering.
decision_changed: Makes quantifier, annotation and filtering sensitivity mandatory when interpreting lncRNAs or other low-abundance features.
constraints: lncRNA-focused evidence; does not establish a universal preprocessing winner for all gene-level analyses.
skill_action: Create a feature-generation passport and repeat key lncRNA results across defensible annotations/quantifiers.
writing_requirement: Methods: annotation, quantifier and filtering; Results: detection/sensitivity comparison; Legend: feature universe; Discussion: low-expression and annotation dependence.

title: Monod: model-based discovery and integration through fitting stochastic transcriptional dynamics to single-cell sequencing data
concrete_content: Fits stochastic transcriptional dynamics to nascent and mature RNA counts to separate technical and biological variation without relying on opaque normalized embeddings.
decision_changed: Requires kinetic claims to use compatible molecular layers and explicit biophysical assumptions rather than generic normalized expression.
constraints: Needs reliable nascent/mature information and model adequacy; inferred parameters are not direct rates or observed time.
skill_action: Audit count layers and assumptions; compare kinetic conclusions with simpler expression summaries and sensitivity fits.
writing_requirement: Methods: molecular layers, likelihood and diagnostics; Results: parameter uncertainty; Legend: inferred quantities; Discussion: identifiability and assay limitations.

title: Feature selection methods affect the performance of scRNA-seq data integration and querying
concrete_content: Shows that HVG method, feature number and batch/lineage-aware selection change integration, label transfer, query mapping and unseen-population detection.
decision_changed: Moves feature selection from an invisible default to a task-fitted model component requiring held-out sensitivity.
constraints: Rankings are task and dataset dependent; label leakage and reference coverage can change apparent performance.
skill_action: Prespecify feature-selection purpose; compare feature counts/methods; evaluate unseen populations and leave-dataset-out queries.
writing_requirement: Methods: feature rule, number and fit scope; Results: preservation/query sensitivity; Legend: feature set; Discussion: task-specific dependence.

title: Recovery of biological signals lost in single-cell batch integration with CellANOVA
concrete_content: Demonstrates that integration can remove biological signal and uses a pool-of-controls design to recover biologically relevant variation.
decision_changed: Requires biological-preservation checks alongside batch mixing and makes experimental controls central to identifiable correction.
constraints: Cannot recover a biological effect fully confounded with batch; control-pool assumptions must fit the design.
skill_action: Audit biology-batch balance; compare unintegrated counts and integrated space; stop if effect is non-identifiable.
writing_requirement: Methods: control pool, integration purpose and preservation metrics; Results: recovered/lost signals; Legend: corrected versus raw layer; Discussion: confounding boundary.

title: scvi-hub: an actionable repository for model-driven single-cell analysis
concrete_content: Provides discoverable pretrained probabilistic single-cell models for atlas reuse, annotation, imputation and deconvolution workflows.
decision_changed: Makes checkpoint, reference provenance, preprocessing compatibility and domain coverage part of the analysis contract.
constraints: Repository availability does not establish validity; reference/model bias and distribution mismatch remain.
skill_action: Audit checkpoint/corpus overlap and compatibility; require query uncertainty and simple task-specific baselines.
writing_requirement: Methods: model/checkpoint, corpus and preprocessing; Results: held-out transfer and uncertainty; Legend: model-derived values; Discussion: reference-domain limits.

title: Benchmarking algorithms for single-cell multi-omics prediction and integration
concrete_content: Benchmarks 14 prediction and 18 integration algorithms across 47 datasets and vertical, horizontal and mosaic multi-omic configurations.
decision_changed: Requires integration evaluation to match the actual data configuration and downstream task rather than quote a single overall rank.
constraints: Multi-omics-specific; not a universal pure-scRNA batch-correction ranking and performance depends on modality/configuration.
skill_action: Classify the integration configuration; use task-matched metrics and held-out datasets; do not extrapolate rankings.
writing_requirement: Methods: configuration, modalities and metrics; Results: task-specific performance; Legend: measured versus predicted modality; Discussion: benchmark transfer limits.

title: Deep generative modeling of sample-level heterogeneity in single-cell genomics
concrete_content: MrVI models sample-level heterogeneity without prespecified cell states and illustrates stratification in COVID-19, IBD and perturbation cohorts.
decision_changed: Elevates sample-level latent structure as a cohort estimand while preserving the biological sample as the inferential unit.
constraints: Latent groups are hypotheses; external meaning, stability and validation are required and cells do not increase patient n.
skill_action: Define sample-level target; perform donor/site holdouts and latent-state stability; validate strata externally.
writing_requirement: Methods: sample hierarchy, model and splits; Results: sample-level uncertainty/replication; Legend: donor-level points; Discussion: exploratory latent-group meaning.

title: Consensus prediction of cell type labels in single-cell data with popV
concrete_content: Combines multiple annotation methods with ontology-aware consensus voting and uncertainty reporting.
decision_changed: Requires consensus/confidence and an unknown option rather than treating one transferred label as ground truth.
constraints: Dependent on reference and ontology coverage; novel or rare states can be forcibly assigned.
skill_action: Build a marker-reference-consensus evidence matrix; review low-confidence labels manually and preserve unknowns.
writing_requirement: Methods: reference, ontology, voters and confidence; Results: concordance/unresolved fraction; Legend: label source; Discussion: reference coverage.

title: CASSIA: a multi-agent large language model for automated and interpretable cell annotation
concrete_content: Uses a multi-agent LLM workflow for annotation across 970 cell types with explicit reasoning, quality assessment, confidence and hallucination controls.
decision_changed: Allows LLMs as auditable proposal generators but requires their reasoning to be checked against markers, references and uncertainty.
constraints: Model/prompt and knowledge bias; fluent reasoning is not evidence and rare/novel cells need manual review.
skill_action: Version prompts/models; cite marker evidence; compare reference/consensus labels; assign unknown when confidence is low.
writing_requirement: Methods: model/prompt/version and inputs; Results: concordance/confidence; Legend: LLM-derived labels; Discussion: hallucination and knowledge limits.

title: Reproducible single-cell annotation of programs underlying T cell subsets, activation states and functions
concrete_content: TCAT/starCAT derives reproducible continuous T-cell programs from about 1.7 million cells across 700 individuals and 38 tissues.
decision_changed: Requires continuous activation/function programs to be separated from discrete subtype identity.
constraints: Core validation is T-cell centered; a program score is not a distinct lineage or universal cell type.
skill_action: Annotate class and program separately; test program stability by donor/tissue and avoid forced subtype splits.
writing_requirement: Methods: program derivation/reference; Results: donor/tissue reproducibility; Legend: score versus label; Discussion: T-cell and continuum limits.

title: mcRigor: a statistical method to enhance the rigor of metacell partitioning in single-cell data analysis
concrete_content: Uses double-permutation statistical testing to assess metacell homogeneity and tune partitioning methods/hyperparameters.
decision_changed: Prevents metacells from being accepted as homogeneous simply because an algorithm produced them.
constraints: Applies to metacell partitions; genuine biological continua may appear heterogeneous and test validity depends on null assumptions.
skill_action: Test partition homogeneity; compare hyperparameters; exclude unstable metacells from primary aggregation.
writing_requirement: Methods: partition and null/permutation; Results: homogeneity/stability; Legend: metacell composition; Discussion: continuum and null-model limits.

title: Benchmarking scRNA-seq copy number variation callers
concrete_content: Benchmarks six RNA-CNV callers on 21 datasets against scWGS/WES truth and shows strong dependence on reference cells, allelic information and data size.
decision_changed: Makes RNA-CNV supporting evidence rather than malignancy truth and requires orthogonal validation for decisive clone claims.
constraints: RNA expression is an indirect CNV signal; reference contamination, coverage and caller choice alter results.
skill_action: Audit normal reference and caller sensitivity; report concordance; validate key malignancy/clone assignments with DNA/pathology.
writing_requirement: Methods: caller, reference and DNA truth; Results: concordance/uncertainty; Legend: RNA-derived CNV; Discussion: not DNA truth.

title: Method of moments framework for differential expression analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing data
concrete_content: Memento estimates condition effects on expression mean, variability and gene-gene correlation at large scale.
decision_changed: Broadens DE estimands beyond the mean while requiring grouping, uncertainty and multiplicity to be explicit.
constraints: Results depend on grouping/design and adequate biological replication; moment changes are associations, not mechanisms.
skill_action: Choose mean/variability/correlation estimand; test donor consistency; correct the declared family of hypotheses.
writing_requirement: Methods: estimand, groups and design; Results: effect/interval/FDR; Legend: moment and biological n; Discussion: association and replication limits.

title: Transcriptome-wide analysis of differential expression in perturbation atlases
concrete_content: TRADE models the distribution of true transcriptome-wide perturbation effects separately from estimation error and reveals impacts missed by standard tests.
decision_changed: Adds a transcriptome-wide perturbation-impact estimand instead of equating the number of significant genes with effect magnitude.
constraints: Perturbation-atlas specific; aggregate impact does not replace gene-level effects, target engagement or donor-level inference.
skill_action: Report both transcriptome-wide and gene-level effects; model estimation error; verify controls and perturbation efficiency.
writing_requirement: Methods: perturbation design and error model; Results: aggregate plus gene effects; Legend: estimand; Discussion: atlas-specific scope.

title: FLASH-MM: fast and scalable single-cell differential expression analysis using linear mixed-effects models
concrete_content: Uses scalable linear mixed-effects models to account for sample correlation and individual variation with benchmarked false-positive control and power.
decision_changed: Makes sample correlation explicit when cell-level modeling is used and rejects cells-as-independent-n analyses.
constraints: Requires model diagnostics and sufficient samples; rare states remain low powered despite many cells.
skill_action: Specify random/fixed effects; inspect calibration and donor influence; compare with pseudobulk sensitivity.
writing_requirement: Methods: formula, random effects and diagnostics; Results: effect/interval/donor stability; Legend: patient n; Discussion: rare-state power.

title: HiDDEN: a machine learning method for detection of disease-relevant populations in case-control single-cell transcriptomics data
concrete_content: Refines case-control sample labels to probabilistic cell-level disease relevance and detects small or mildly affected subsets.
decision_changed: Prevents copying case status to every cell and treats disease relevance as a weak-label inference requiring validation.
constraints: Probabilistic output can be circular if evaluated with reused markers; depends on controls and independent validation.
skill_action: Audit negative controls and label leakage; report probabilities/uncertainty; validate nominated cells independently.
writing_requirement: Methods: weak labels, controls and splits; Results: cell subset plus donor replication; Legend: inferred probability; Discussion: not cell truth.

title: Annotation-free discovery of disease-relevant cells in single-cell datasets
concrete_content: Uses multiple-instance learning from patient-level labels to identify rare disease-relevant cells, including minimal residual disease settings across tissues/time points.
decision_changed: Makes rare-cell discovery possible without fixed annotation while retaining patient bags as the supervised unit.
constraints: Evidence is strongly leukemia/CyTOF/scRNA oriented; needs negative bags, leakage control and disease-specific revalidation.
skill_action: Define patient bags and held-out donors; verify rare cells with markers/orthogonal assays; preserve annotation-free status.
writing_requirement: Methods: bag construction, splits and controls; Results: patient-level performance/rare-cell rate; Legend: inferred cells; Discussion: disease-transfer limit.

title: Single-cell trajectory inference for detecting transient events in biological processes
concrete_content: scTransient uses wavelet-based scoring to detect transient events along an upstream supervised pseudotime.
decision_changed: Requires transient-event claims to inherit and report uncertainty from the chosen pseudotime and window/scale.
constraints: Upstream ordering error, window choice and signal-to-noise can generate or hide transient events; pseudotime is not observed time.
skill_action: Test roots/orderings and wavelet scales; confirm transient markers in measured time or orthogonal assays.
writing_requirement: Methods: pseudotime, supervision and scale; Results: event stability; Legend: inferred axis; Discussion: ordering/SNR limits.

title: Interpretable trajectory inference with single-cell linear adaptive negative-binomial expression (scLANE) testing
concrete_content: Provides interpretable negative-binomial trajectory expression testing with splines and GEE/GLMM support for multi-subject designs.
decision_changed: Makes subject-aware trajectory testing and interpretable gene curves preferable to cell-only trend p values.
constraints: Operates downstream of a chosen pseudotime/trajectory; root and ordering errors propagate into gene tests.
skill_action: Use multi-subject design; vary roots/trajectories; report curve uncertainty and donor-level consistency.
writing_requirement: Methods: trajectory, spline and subject model; Results: curve/effect/FDR; Legend: inferred pseudotime; Discussion: upstream-order dependence.

title: ArchVelo: archetypal velocity modeling for single-cell multi-omic trajectories
concrete_content: Combines paired chromatin accessibility and RNA through archetypal velocity modeling to infer trajectories, latent time and candidate transcription factors.
decision_changed: Restricts ArchVelo use to paired multiome data and separates TF nomination from validated regulation.
constraints: Not an scRNA-only velocity method; paired-modality quality and kinetic assumptions matter; TF hypotheses require perturbation.
skill_action: Verify pairing and modality QC; test trajectory sensitivity; validate candidate TFs experimentally.
writing_requirement: Methods: paired data, kinetics and archetypes; Results: stability/uncertainty; Legend: inferred velocity/time; Discussion: no fate or TF causality claim.

title: Inferring cell differentiation maps from lineage tracing data
concrete_content: Carta optimizes differentiation maps from single-cell lineage-tracing trees while permitting convergent differentiation and unobserved progenitors.
decision_changed: Requires lineage claims to use lineage measurements and allows non-tree state maps when biology supports convergence.
constraints: Needs reliable lineage trees; barcode/tree errors propagate and it cannot be applied to expression snapshots alone.
skill_action: Audit lineage-tree quality; compare map constraints; distinguish observed barcodes from inferred progenitors.
writing_requirement: Methods: lineage assay/tree and optimization; Results: map support/sensitivity; Legend: observed versus inferred nodes; Discussion: tracing-error limits.

title: Dissecting crosstalk induced by cell-cell communication using single-cell transcriptomic data
concrete_content: SigXTalk links receptors, transcription factors and target genes in hypergraphs to nominate pathway crosstalk, including time-course applications.
decision_changed: Raises the evidentiary bar from ligand-receptor co-expression to a coherent receptor-TF-target hypothesis while retaining causal limits.
constraints: Depends on expression and network priors; does not demonstrate physical contact, signal flow or causality.
skill_action: Check donor replication and prior versions; test downstream targets; add spatial/protein and perturbation validation.
writing_requirement: Methods: databases, hypergraph and null; Results: supported paths/effects; Legend: inferred edges; Discussion: compatibility not causality.

title: FastCCC: a permutation-free framework for scalable, robust, and reference-based cell-cell communication analysis in single cell transcriptomics studies
concrete_content: Uses analytical p values and modular algebra for scalable CCC and supplies a reference panel built from roughly 16 million cells across 19 tissues.
decision_changed: Separates computational scalability/significance from biological effect and makes reference-panel provenance explicit.
constraints: Reference/model bias persists; analytical p values are not effect sizes, donor replication or causal signaling.
skill_action: Report effect and donor consistency; audit reference compatibility; validate top sender-receiver hypotheses orthogonally.
writing_requirement: Methods: reference, algebra/null and aggregation; Results: effect plus significance; Legend: sample n and inferred edge; Discussion: reference/causal limits.

title: D-SPIN constructs regulatory network models from scRNA-seq that reveal organizing principles of perturbation response
concrete_content: Constructs interpretable generative regulatory models across thousands of perturbations and predicts state proportions including unseen dose combinations.
decision_changed: Connects observed perturbation responses to testable network hypotheses while requiring interpolation/OOD and identifiability checks.
constraints: Network non-identifiability and context dependence; unseen dose combinations are predictions until tested.
skill_action: Compare network edges across perturbations; test dose holdouts/simple baselines; validate prioritized regulators experimentally.
writing_requirement: Methods: perturbations, model and holdouts; Results: edge/dose uncertainty; Legend: observed versus predicted; Discussion: hypothesis and interpolation limits.

title: PSGRN: Gene regulatory network inference from single-cell perturbational data through self-training with synthetic gold standards
concrete_content: Combines interventional and observational single-cell data with self-training on synthetic gold standards and evaluation using CausalBench.
decision_changed: Prioritizes interventional support for GRN edges while forcing explicit discussion of the truth set used for training/evaluation.
constraints: Synthetic priors and available ground truth are incomplete; precision/recall may not transfer to new biological contexts.
skill_action: Audit synthetic-gold construction and overlap; validate edges in independent perturbations and functional assays.
writing_requirement: Methods: interventions, synthetic standards and benchmark split; Results: edge precision/recall; Legend: evidence type; Discussion: incomplete-truth limit.

title: Decoding heterogeneous single-cell perturbation responses
concrete_content: Introduces a perturbation-response score to resolve partial knockdown, dose and buffered versus sensitive single-cell responses.
decision_changed: Makes heterogeneous target engagement part of the estimand rather than averaging all guide-positive cells.
constraints: Score is relative and can reflect efficiency or confounding; needs controls and experimental validation.
skill_action: Quantify target engagement; stratify response; model dose/efficiency; validate sensitive and buffered states.
writing_requirement: Methods: score, controls, dose and efficiency; Results: response distribution; Legend: score interpretation; Discussion: relative/confounded response.

title: GPerturb: Gaussian process modelling of single-cell perturbation data
concrete_content: Uses sparse Gaussian processes to estimate gene-level effects and uncertainty for discrete and continuous perturbations.
decision_changed: Requires uncertainty-aware effect estimation and accommodates continuous perturbation intensity instead of binary guide status alone.
constraints: Additive/kernel assumptions may miss high-order nonlinear effects; uncertainty is conditional on the fitted model.
skill_action: Audit kernel/model fit; compare dose representations and simple baselines; validate nonlinear/high-effect genes.
writing_requirement: Methods: GP/kernel, dose and approximation; Results: effect/uncertainty; Legend: posterior quantity; Discussion: model-conditional limits.

title: Benchmarking algorithms for generalizable single-cell perturbation response prediction
concrete_content: Benchmarks 27 methods on 29 datasets across unseen-context and unseen-perturbation scenarios, including foundation models.
decision_changed: Requires scenario-specific OOD splits and simple baselines; no model may be called generally predictive from one random-cell split.
constraints: Rankings depend on scenario/data; unseen-perturbation prediction remains difficult and aggregate metrics can hide gene failures.
skill_action: Define held-out domain; prevent leakage; add linear/control baselines and gene/pathway/distribution metrics.
writing_requirement: Methods: splits, baselines and metrics; Results: scenario-stratified performance; Legend: seen/unseen status; Discussion: OOD failures.

title: Systematic reconstruction of molecular pathway signatures using scalable single-cell perturbation screens
concrete_content: Screens more than 1,500 perturbations in six cell lines and five contexts, using Mixscale to handle perturbation efficiency and derive conserved pathway signatures.
decision_changed: Requires pathway signatures to account for perturbation efficiency and be tested across cellular contexts before transfer.
constraints: Cell-line/context specific; conservation across screened lines does not establish patient-tissue validity.
skill_action: Audit efficiency adjustment; compare contexts; freeze signatures and recalibrate/validate in tissue or patient data.
writing_requirement: Methods: screen, contexts and efficiency model; Results: cross-context conservation; Legend: cell line/perturbation n; Discussion: patient-transfer limit.

title: Systema: a framework for evaluating genetic perturbation response prediction beyond systematic variation
concrete_content: Shows across ten datasets, three technologies and five cell lines that systematic perturbed-control variation and perturbation selection can inflate response-prediction metrics.
decision_changed: Makes perturbation-specific signal beyond systematic variation a mandatory evaluation target.
constraints: Evaluation framework rather than a predictive model; controlling variation does not solve unseen-perturbation generalization.
skill_action: Apply variation-aware controls; reconstruct perturbation/dataset splits; report baseline-relative gene-level performance.
writing_requirement: Methods: systematic-variation control and selection; Results: corrected versus naive metrics; Legend: evaluation target; Discussion: residual generalization limit.

title: scDrugMap: benchmarking large foundation models for drug response prediction
concrete_content: Benchmarks eight single-cell foundation models and two LLMs on about 495,000 cells from 60 datasets under pooled, cross-dataset, fine-tuned and zero-shot drug-response settings.
decision_changed: Prevents a single winner claim across transfer settings and requires evaluation mode to be named explicitly.
constraints: Cancer drug-response focus; accuracy does not establish calibration, mechanism, prospective benefit or other-disease transfer.
skill_action: Stratify by transfer setting; audit dataset overlap; compare specialist baselines; report calibration and prospective test needs.
writing_requirement: Methods: models, corpus overlap and setting; Results: setting-specific baseline-relative metrics; Legend: zero-shot/fine-tuned status; Discussion: domain/prospective limits.

title: Evaluating the role of pretraining dataset size and diversity on single-cell foundation model performance
concrete_content: Evaluates 400 models in 6,400 experiments over 22.2 million cells and finds early performance plateaus with no clear universal scaling law in tested settings.
decision_changed: Rejects model/data size as a proxy for utility and requires task-level evidence against smaller/simple baselines.
constraints: Conclusion is bounded to tested architectures, objectives, corpora and tasks; future methods may scale differently.
skill_action: Audit task fit and corpus diversity/overlap; compare smaller models and baselines; select by held-out utility and compute.
writing_requirement: Methods: corpus, model sizes/objectives and tasks; Results: scaling curves/uncertainty; Legend: data/model scale; Discussion: tested-scope boundary.
